notes: Canonical fleet app + coding-seat inventory.  onboard-new-app.sh adds a row here, then patches the registries listed in docs/ONBOARDING-NEW-APP.md.  check-fleet-registry.py verifies those files still mention every app.  GROK-BOT is a fleet-wide identity that drives Cursor cloud agents; it shares CURSOR's folder name and gets no lanes of its own.  Seats carry zulipBotEmail and zulipFileCode, copied from the roster in docs/protocols/zulip-fleet-guide.md (the file code must match the simple-chat CLI's rule).  A retired seat has no bot, and aliasOf names the live seat that a retired alias now means.  Each app's acronym is also its Linear team key (Linear replaced THE BOARD, owner 2026-10-10).  liveBoard is the file name of the app's archived effort log under appsRoot; it is a record only, and nothing creates or checks that file any more.

apps.notes: Friendly adaptation of @deepseek-ai/dsh for DSH and MiniMax parity (formerly named Harness; renamed to Clutch 2026-09-30).  Always-on pm2 clutch-web on 127.0.0.1:3180.  Live install ~/apps/clutch-runtime (a real standalone clone of origin/main, updated by scripts/update-mac-app.sh), state in ~/.clutch.  Canonical npm package (clutch) for BotFleet's DSH driver.  App acronym C (owner 2026-10-23, AFC-333):  C-n is a Clutch Linear issue and C#n a Clutch PR, replacing CLUTCH;  the seat tag stays CLUTCH.

No digestColor:  the daily digest's --cc colour (#0d9488) is already congress-trading-shared's, and check-fleet-registry.py rejects a reused colour.  The acronym CC and the repo-cc badge come from REPO_BADGE in scripts/build-fleet-daily-digest.py.  CC is also CodeCaps's Linear team key, and the CC# Zulip linkifier points at CodeCaps (owner 2026-10-16, AFC-336;  CAPS# is an alias).

Expiring artifact sharing and static hosting (fleetlink.online, fleetlink.app) with an iOS App Clip.  Public repo.  No digestColor and no digest badge:  FleetLink is not on the public-activity allowlist (scripts/public_activity_repos.py), so the daily digest and the calendar do not list it.  The acronym FL was chosen on 2026-10-11 (AFC-252):  no other registry row, Linear team key or Zulip linkifier uses it, and Jay creates the Linear team FL.  FL#n links to FleetLink issues and FL-n to its Linear team (zulip-fleet-guide.md, Current Linkifiers).  The live fleetlink.online worker (fleet-share-api) is still built from fleetlink-legacy until cutover, so a fix to production today lands there.

LEGACY, in maintenance until cutover.  Private repo of the live fleet-share-api worker that serves fleetlink.online and fleetlink.app (its wrangler.toml routes both zones);  the P0 auth hotfix of 2026-10-08 landed here.  Its row exists so lane new can make hotfix lanes.  Retire it with the Offboarding steps in docs/ONBOARDING-NEW-APP.md when FleetLink replaces it.  FLL is a registry key only and Jay may rename it:  no Linear team (file a hotfix under FL or AFC), no Zulip linkifier (FLL#n would link to a repo named FLL, so use fleetlink-legacy#n), no digestColor and no public feed.  Its integration tree is ~/Code/fleetlink-legacy, a plain clone of origin/main that agents never edit.

The fleet marketing repo:  the static catalog at https://simplewithus.com/ and one page per app.  It holds no product code;  each shipped tool lives in its own fleet repo.  Its row exists so lane new can make marketing-site lanes (AFC-297), and it is the reason the handbook records the swu lane prefix.  SWU is a registry key and the Linear team for Simple With Us website work.  No digestColor, no badge class and no public-activity feed:  it is not a shipped app, and a digest row for the catalog would crowd out the tools it lists.  Its integration tree is ~/Code/Simple-With-Us, reset by a daemon, so all agent work happens in a lane.

seats.notes: Grok on the web and the iOS app: a cloud seat with no Mac lanes or checkouts (owner 2026-10-08).  Held by the server listener, not the Mac one (docs/protocols/agent-sync-partition.toml).  No branch prefix, as in the FLEET-PROTOCOL.md Active Seats table, so lane refuses it before it makes a worktree.  The tag GROK-WEB makes grok-web a seat token whatever the suffix is (layout.py derives an alias from the lowercase tag), so a GROK lane slug may not start with web-, as grok plus build is GROK-BUILD's.  GROK-WEB makes no lanes, so nothing else is affected.

Grok Bot, one fleet-wide identity:  the GB-<ROLE> personas (Zulip bots <role>-grok-bot@) that implement through Cursor cloud agents.  It opens no Mac lanes, so it has no branch prefix of its own (it carried CURSOR's cursor/ until 2026-10-11, which put one prefix on two seats).  worktreeSuffix stays cursor, so the lane tool still refuses GROK-BOT and still reads gb and grok-bot as the cursor folder.  A cursor/ branch can come from CURSOR or from a GB persona's Cursor cloud agent, so the prefix alone does not name the seat.  Its app is in seatApps, not here.

seats.notes: Meta Muse cloud VM batch compute & creative assistant (dispatched via Mac/iOS apps; unmetered VM compute for multi-day transcoding/batch tasks). Formerly tagged MUSE.
Meta AI interactive terminal coding agent (muse CLI / Muse Code). Distinct from Muse Assist ([MA]).

OpenCode (opencode CLI, ~/.local/bin/opencode, global rules file ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md).  A seat since the owner's decision of Sat, Oct 10, 2026 ("opencode as a seat"); before that OpenCode was an engine-only CLI with no default seat.  Any provider or model OpenCode runs is still OPENCODE.  A BotFleet bot that runs on the opencode engine keeps its BF-<ROLE> seat, and a launcher's AGENT_LAUNCH_SEAT wins over the platform default.

Echo, shown as Echo (Instinct):  one of the two bots of the Instinct app (instinct.com), which runs on its own computer and reaches the fleet through the hosted ST-MCP bridge, not through a Mac lane.  Held by the server listener (docs/protocols/agent-sync-partition.toml).  Does PR troubleshooting and release work;  its merged Congress.Trade PRs so far were pushed on instinct/ branches under the owner's GitHub login, so GitHub cannot tell the two bots apart.  echo/ is its own prefix from now on.  Has its own Linear app, Echo (Instinct), key variables LINEAR_ECHO_CLIENT_ID and LINEAR_ECHO_CLIENT_SECRET.  Registered Sun, Oct 11, 2026 (owner: add the rows).

The other bot of the Instinct app, shown as Wise (Instinct) since Sun, Oct 11, 2026 (the owner's name for what used to be called the Instinct version).  The seat tag is WISE (owner 2026-10-15);  INSTINCT is retired and stays as an accepted spelling so existing references keep resolving.  instinct/ remains a branch prefix alongside wise/ because its merged work is on instinct/ branches under the owner's GitHub login.  Held by the server listener (docs/protocols/agent-sync-partition.toml), reached through the hosted ST-MCP bridge, and makes no Mac lanes.  Has its own Linear app, Wise (Instinct), key variables LINEAR_WISE_CLIENT_ID and LINEAR_WISE_CLIENT_SECRET.  A launcher's AGENT_LAUNCH_SEAT wins over any default.

seatApps.notes: The app each seat runs in, for code that counts apps instead of models (a consult quorum) or asks which product a seat tag belongs to.  Kept out of seats on purpose:  a dozen tools read seats and a row there makes lanes, skill copies and listener seats.  bySeat has one entry per live row of seats (check-fleet-registry.py enforces it).  extraSeats are real seats with no row in seats (hosted or owner-run).  patterns cover the families whose tags are made up of a role (BF-<ROLE> and GB-<ROLE>).  scripts/agent_sync/identity.py strict_seat() and seat_app() read it;  canonical_seat() does not.

sessionIds.notes: AFC-361 (owner, Oct 19):  board writes, notes_create and notes_update, and apple-notes-coding.sh carry a session id, so resume-wake (docs/protocols/resume-wake-safety-design.md section 4) can find a seat's session for a topic.  A writer takes the id from its explicit flag or argument, then AGENT_SESSION, then its platform's variable in envBySeat (a seat with no entry there tries every variable in fallbackEnv, in order), and refuses when it finds none, unless the writer's resolved seat is exempt.  Exempt seats have one thread with the owner, so there is no session id or thread name to pass:  Grok bots (GROK-BOT and GB-*), MA (Rob), JET (Jet, OpenAI dot), WISE and ECHO (Instinct).  The exemption is decided from the resolved seat (AGENT_SEAT, a launcher's AGENT_LAUNCH_SEAT, the per-call identity, or a relay sender), never from a flag the caller sets.  scripts/linear-board/board, scripts/apple-notes-coding.sh, scripts/agent_sync/session_ids.py and scripts/agent-sync-mcp/src/session-ids.js carry copies of this block, and scripts/test_session_ids_parity.py keeps them equal.  Platforms with no variable of their own (FX, Clutch, AG, MC, GROK-WEB) pass --session or set AGENT_SESSION.
